Definition: from Δημήτηρ (Ceres); Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian:--Demetrius.
BiblicalUsage: Demetrius is the name of two men: the silversmith of Ephesus who made silver shrines for Diana and stirred the riot against Paul, and the Christian of whom John writes that he has a good report of all men and of the truth itself. One name, a persecutor and a witness, and the contrast is the whole story.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Demetrius shows that a name is not a destiny: the silversmith fought the gospel for his trade, and the Christian lived it for the truth. My position is that the report of all men is worth having, and it is earned by a life, not bought with silver.
RelatedPeople: Paul; Demetrius, the Silversmith; Demetrius (3 John)
